newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - MOROCCO ECONOMIC WEEKLIES - JAN 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - MOROCCO ECONOMIC WEEKLIES - JAN 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's weekly economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The administrative division of Casablanca into 35 local councils has caused financial imbalances among them as some are wealthier than others, while the multiplication of those responsible for taking decisions is preventing big projects going ahead.

- An expert at France's International Research and Studies Council (CNRS) says reforms taken so far are not part of a real economic policy. "I do not think Morocco will become an emerging country and really take off ... there is an openness but it cannot become a dragon ... the 55 percent illiteracy rate is a reminder of the gap between a small elite and the rest of the population."

- Monetary authorities keep political pressure on banks to reduce interest rates for small and medium-sized enterprises. Story says banks with profitability below 10 percent will be prey to bigger banks.

- Growth is back but this is due mainly to an exceptional harvest. It will be difficult to achieve the same performances in 1977 since only 60 percent of the land has been sown. Forecasts are for a 3.0 percent growth but it is still not enough to sustain the economy.

- Forecasts say gross domestic product will grow by 3.0 percent in 1997 but high unemployment and insufficient investments delay economic development. Debate in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) over an investment treaty shows up Morocco's delay in privatisation strategies and in ways to lure foreign capital.

- Promising year for investments with the convention signed by the finance ministry and banks to boost investments, with plans by the banks to reduce interest rates on firms and reforms to expand the stock exchange.
